note: Adapted from Coaton's (1955) detailed account of 4 soldiers from the Congo (in English), which agrees with Sjöstedt's (1926) brief original description and is broadly consistent with Grassé's description and figures; Coaton also gives a comparison table with the Ghana and Ivory Coast series. No alate was seen (that paper names an alate as collarti instead). The original gives the body length as 114—127, which judging by the decimal places of the other measurements in the same paper should be 11.4—12.7 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head yellowish brown in dorsal view, the antennal carinae darker; postclypeal region yellowish brown, anteclypeus white, labrum yellowish brown. Base of the mandibles dark yellowish brown, the rest glossy black. Antennae pale yellowish brown at the base, grading to creamy yellow towards the tip. Compound eyes and ocelli reduced and white. Postmentum yellowish brown with a pale brown band on either side. Sides of the pronotum creamy yellow, the middle yellowish brown, the anterior margin with a fine brown edge. Rest of the thorax and nota pale creamy yellow, the sternites creamy white. Femora creamy white; tibiae and tarsi creamy yellow, the apical tibial spurs and tarsal claws dark brown. Head, thorax and abdomen sparsely hairy. Head elongate-rectangular in dorsal view, the sides straight and parallel or slightly concave in the middle, the posterolateral angles broadly rounded. Cranial and transverse sutures clear, the frontoclypeal suture appearing as a transverse depression. Ocelli as minute dots, reduced but visible; compound eyes oval, unpigmented and reduced. Frons depressed in the middle, bounded behind by a distinct concave arcuate ridge; in lateral view the frons slopes forwards and downwards from the vertex at about 30°. Sides of the anteclypeus straight and converging towards the tip, the anterior margin slightly concave. Sides of the labrum straight and slightly divergent, passing into a straight anterior margin that is slightly raised in the middle, with a few bristles on or near the anterior margin. Mandibles stout, the tip curved upwards in lateral view; in dorsal view the mandibles are raised on the outer side at the base, then the sides curve inwards towards the tip. Right mandible with 2 prominent marginal teeth: the first step-like, about at the midpoint, with a trace of a second small point near its proximal end, the cutting edge beyond the first tooth slightly serrate with 3 or 4 small points; the second parenthesis-shaped with a small backward point near the middle. Left mandible with 3 distinct marginal teeth: the first acute and narrow at the base; the second broad at the base with a distinct point near the tip and another less distinct point near the sharp notch that separates it from the third tooth; the third broad at the base and parenthesis-shaped with a small point near the tip and another more prominent point slightly beyond the middle. Antennae 13—17-segmented (8 specimens examined: 2 incomplete, 2 with 13, 1 with 14, 2 with 15, 1 with 17); segment 2 from about half the length of the club-like segment 3 in the 13-segmented form to only slightly shorter than the barely clavate segment 3 in the 17-segmented form; segments 4 and 5 about equal, equal to or slightly shorter than segment 2. Pronotum transversely arched, about as wide as, slightly wider or slightly narrower than the head (2.33 against 2.33; 2.33 against 2.31; 2.19 against 2.29; 2.17 against 2.21); length along the midline slightly more or slightly less than half the width (1.04 against 2.33; 1.17 against 2.19; 1.04 against 2.33; 1.00 against 2.17); anterior margin concave, the anterolateral angles almost square and broadly rounded; sides only slightly convex, passing at an obtuse angle into the flat posterior margin, which is slightly concave medially. Meso- and metanota with reduced wing pads, the posterior margin slightly concave in the middle only. Apical tibial spurs of the fore, middle and hind legs all 3. Cerci short. All 4 soldiers examined have styli.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Measurements of the Congo specimens (4 soldiers): body length 114—127 (mean 121), head including mandibles 5.04—5.71 (mean 5.50), head width 2.21—2.33 (mean 2.28), left mandible length 1.92—2.04 (mean 1.97), pronotum length 1.00—1.17 (mean 1.06), width 2.17—2.33 (mean 2.27), antennae 13—17-segmented. Compared with the Ghana type series (head including mandibles 5.4—6.0) and the Ivory Coast series (4.6—4.7), the Congo specimens are closer to the former in head-plus-mandible length. Distribution: Aburi, Ghana (type locality), Bingerville, Ivory Coast, Kawa forest, Democratic Republic of the Congo (Lake Albert).
